hook: 2026's framework map was redrawn in eight months — AutoGen and Semantic Kernel merged into **Microsoft Agent Framework**, LangGraph went 1.0, first-party SDKs matured. The tour, honestly given.

scenes.title: What changed: three structural shifts
scenes.sub: Why last year's map misleads this year's decisions
scenes.narration: Between October 2025 and mid-2026, the landscape consolidated around three shifts. ONE — vendor consolidation: Microsoft put AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into maintenance mode and merged both into the Microsoft Agent Framework — MAF — which hit 1.0 GA in April 2026 for Python and .NET simultaneously; LangChain and LangGraph reached 1.0 the same October week, making LangGraph the graph-runtime standard. TWO — protocols went open and changed the switching math: MCP moved to Linux Foundation stewardship, A2A crossed 150-plus adopting organizations, and the industry shorthand settled — MCP for tools, A2A for agents; integrations built on MCP port between frameworks almost trivially. THREE — first-party SDKs matured: OpenAI's Agents SDK went GA in March 2026 with sandbox execution; the Claude Agent SDK hardened for long-running autonomous work. The practical consequence: framework choice matters less than it did, because the protocols underneath carry your integrations.

items.s: AutoGen + Semantic Kernel → Agent Framework 1.0 (Apr 2026) · native MCP + A2A · .NET + Python
MCP under Linux Foundation · A2A 150+ orgs · 'MCP for tools, A2A for agents'
OpenAI Agents SDK GA (Mar 2026) · Claude Agent SDK · Google ADK 2.0 multi-language

scenes.narration: The maintenance-mode nuance, stated precisely because it decides migrations: 'maintenance mode' means bug and security fixes continue — nothing breaks — but no new features ever; MCP, A2A, and any future protocol work lands only in the successor. So AutoGen and Semantic Kernel keep RUNNING, but building new capability on them means building on a ceiling. Existing deployments deserve a deliberate migration plan, not panic — and the migration target for Microsoft-ecosystem teams is obvious: MAF inherits both lineages, keeps the conversational patterns AutoGen pioneered, adds Semantic Kernel's enterprise plumbing — sessions, telemetry, middleware — and speaks MCP and A2A natively. For .NET shops, this ended the 'which Microsoft framework' confusion permanently.

scenes.title: LangGraph, MAF, CrewAI: three philosophies
scenes.sub: Graph runtime vs unified enterprise SDK vs role-based crews
scenes.narration: LANGGRAPH — the graph runtime: agents and workflows as explicit state machines — nodes, edges, conditional branching, cycles — with the production essentials built in: checkpointing for durable execution and resume, interrupts for human-in-the-loop, streaming, LangSmith observability. Philosophy: YOU own the control flow; the framework executes it precisely. Best fit: complex, stateful, long-running workflows where determinism and debuggability matter — it powers serious production deployments. MICROSOFT AGENT FRAMEWORK — the unified enterprise SDK: AutoGen's orchestration patterns — sequential, concurrent, handoff, group chat — merged with Semantic Kernel's middleware, sessions, and telemetry; genuinely cross-runtime — Python agents coordinate with .NET agents; native MCP and A2A. Best fit: Microsoft-ecosystem teams — Azure, .NET, existing Semantic Kernel investment — wanting one supported path. CREWAI — role-based crews: agents with roles, goals and backstories organized into crews with processes; the fastest time-to-first-agent and the largest standalone community; pluggable memory, knowledge and RAG backends as of mid-2026. Best fit: rapid prototyping and role-shaped multi-agent tasks — a research crew, a content crew — where structure should emerge from convention, not code.

cards.s: Explicit graphs · checkpoints + interrupts · you own control flow · pairs with LangSmith
AutoGen+SK merged · .NET+Python · MCP+A2A native · enterprise telemetry
Roles + crews · fastest to first agent · largest standalone community · pluggable backends

scenes.narration: How to read the three-way choice. If your problem is a WORKFLOW with loops, branches, and mandatory human gates — LangGraph's explicitness is the point: the graph IS the documentation, and interrupts give you audit points that role-based frameworks approximate. If your problem is enterprise fit — .NET estate, Azure deployment, compliance-shaped telemetry — MAF's lineage merge means one SDK to standardize on, with the cross-runtime story as a genuine differentiator for mixed Python/.NET estates. If your problem is speed and shape — 'a research crew that produces a weekly brief' — CrewAI's conventions get you running in an afternoon. None is universally right; all three are actively maintained as of late 2026 — the ecosystem's healthy tier at the top. The bake-off in AG-16 is how you choose among them with evidence.

scenes.title: First-party SDKs — and the framework you already have
scenes.sub: OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, and plain Python loops
scenes.narration: The vendor SDKs deserve their own look. OPENAI AGENTS SDK — GA March 2026, successor to the archived Swarm project: lightweight primitives — agents, handoffs, guardrails, sessions — plus native sandbox execution across providers; the natural fit when you're standardized on OpenAI models and want the fastest native setup. CLAUDE AGENT SDK — Anthropic's toolkit for agentic work, safety-first design, strong at long-running autonomous sessions and hierarchical subagent spawning; speaks MCP natively. GOOGLE ADK 2.0 — the only major framework with Python, TypeScript, Java and Go SDKs at parity; deep Vertex/Gemini integration and cross-framework agent discovery. And the last option — NO framework: a plain loop with tool definitions — AG-01's thirty lines — plus httpx and asyncio. For narrow, well-understood tasks, this outperforms frameworks on debuggability and dependency surface; many production systems are exactly this, and every framework's abstractions are, ultimately, this loop wearing costumes.

items.s: GA Mar 2026 · handoffs/guardrails/sessions · sandbox execution · best on OpenAI models
Safety-first · long autonomous sessions · subagent spawning · MCP native
Plain loop + tools + httpx · unbeatable debuggability · right size for narrow tasks

scenes.narration: The no-framework path deserves respect rather than embarrassment: frameworks earn their abstractions — checkpoints, interrupts, observability — when your system needs them; a five-tool agent pipeline with known steps needs none of them, and every abstraction is also a failure mode you didn't choose. The pragmatic pattern many teams land on: start no-framework to learn the loop's real shape — you'll feel exactly where checkpoints and handoffs would help — then adopt a framework for the pieces that hurt, often as a library inside your loop rather than a platform underneath it. On vendor SDKs, one caution: their sweetest features tend to assume their own models; multi-provider needs — and the day you need them arrives — are served better by the neutral frameworks. Verify protocol support — MCP, A2A — per SDK before committing; the support matrix shifted fast this year and continues to.

scenes.title: The honest status board, late 2026
scenes.sub: What to build on, what to migrate off
scenes.narration: Consolidating the verified picture. ACTIVELY MAINTAINED — safe foundations: LangGraph 1.0, Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Google ADK, Pydantic AI — the typed, validation-first Python option worth knowing — and Mastra for the TypeScript world. MAINTENANCE MODE — works, ceilinged: AutoGen — community fork AG2 continues separately under its original creators — and Semantic Kernel; both receive fixes, no features, and their own docs point to MAF. ARCHIVED — do not start: OpenAI Swarm, superseded by the Agents SDK. Two verification habits before any commitment: check the repository's pulse — commit cadence, release recency, maintainer responsiveness — and confirm protocol support — MCP and A2A — for YOUR integration needs, because that matrix is still moving. This space ships weekly; the durable lesson is the evaluation METHOD, not today's winner.

items.s: LangGraph · MAF · CrewAI · Agents SDK · Claude Agent SDK · ADK · Pydantic AI · Mastra
AutoGen → MAF or AG2 · Semantic Kernel → MAF · both maintenance-mode since Oct 2025
OpenAI Swarm (archived) · any framework whose repo pulse has flatlined

scenes.narration: A note on how fast this specific board moves: every entry here was verified against late-2026 sources, and several changed within the year — that's WHY the method matters more than the map. When you evaluate, do it in this order: maintenance pulse first — a framework that stops shipping is a future migration whatever its features; protocol support second — MCP-native matters because your tool investments should outlive the framework; ecosystem third — docs, examples, hiring pool. And record your evaluation — the date, the versions, the findings — because 'we chose X in 2026 for reasons R' is exactly the document your successor thanks you for. Framework choice is a two-to-three-year bet; treat it with the seriousness of one, and keep the escape hatches — protocol-based integrations, clean seams — open the whole time.

quiz.q: What does 'maintenance mode' mean for AutoGen and Semantic Kernel?
opts: Bug/security fixes continue, but no new features — new capability lands only in Microsoft Agent Framework
quiz.why: Existing code keeps running, but the ceiling matters for anything you'll maintain past 2027 — plan migration to MAF or AG2.

quiz.q: Why does MCP-native support matter when choosing a framework?
opts: Tool integrations built on MCP port between frameworks almost trivially — your integration investment outlives the framework choice
quiz.why: Protocol-based integrations are the lock-in hedge: they make the framework a replaceable component rather than a permanent decision.

quiz.q: When is the no-framework approach the right choice?
opts: Narrow, well-understood tasks where the plain loop + tools is more debuggable and carries no dependency surface
quiz.why: Frameworks earn their abstractions when you need them; a five-step pipeline with known flow needs none — start plain, adopt frameworks where it hurts.

code.title: The same tiny agent, three ways (shape comparison)
code.body:
# --- 1 · Plain loop (no framework) -------------------------------
while not done and iters < 10:
    msg = llm(messages, tools=TOOLS)
    messages += run_tools(msg)          # ~30 lines total

# --- 2 · LangGraph (explicit graph) -------------------------------
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph
 g = StateGraph(AgentState)
 g.add_node("think", think)
 g.add_node("act", act)
 g.add_conditional_edges("think", route)   # loops visible
 g.add_edge("act", "think")
 graph = g.compile(checkpointer=memory)    # durable + resumable

# --- 3 · Microsoft Agent Framework (conversational) ---------------
from agent_framework.azure import AzureOpenAIChatClient
 agent = AzureOpenAIChatClient().create_agent(
     instructions="…", tools=[…])       # orchestration built-in

# The loop is identical inside all three —
# frameworks differ in who owns the control flow and what comes
# built in (checkpoints, telemetry, handoffs), not in kind.
annot: Same agent, three control-flow owners: you, the graph, the framework
The 30-line loop fitting inside every framework is why no-framework remains legitimate — you can always migrate INTO abstraction
Try all three shapes in the AG-16 bake-off before committing

notes:
# Framework Landscape (verified late 2026)

## Consolidation
- Oct 2025: AutoGen + Semantic Kernel → maintenance mode; LangChain/LangGraph 1.0.
- Apr 3, 2026: **Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0** (Python + .NET), native MCP + A2A.
- Mar 2026: OpenAI Agents SDK GA (Swarm archived). Google ADK 2.0 multi-language.
- MCP → Linux Foundation; A2A 150+ orgs. Shorthand: **MCP = tools, A2A = agents**.

## Contenders
- **LangGraph**: explicit state graphs, checkpoints, interrupts, LangSmith.
- **MAF**: unified enterprise; .NET+Python cross-runtime; telemetry, sessions.
- **CrewAI**: roles/crews, fastest start, largest standalone community.
- Also: Pydantic AI (typed), Mastra (TS), Claude Agent SDK (safety-first).

## Status board
- Build on: LangGraph · MAF · CrewAI · Agents SDK · ADK · Pydantic AI · Mastra.
- Migrate from: AutoGen (→MAF/AG2) · Semantic Kernel (→MAF).
- Never start: Swarm.
- Verify: repo pulse, protocol support, ecosystem — record evaluations with dates.
